Allow.description: One entry of the IR's ``allow`` list.
Allow.title: Allow

Arc.description:
Part of a circle, from ``start_angle`` to ``end_angle``.

The arc runs counterclockwise when ``end_angle`` is larger, clockwise
when it is smaller.
Arc.title: Arc

Between.description: Between two graphs, from ``x[0]`` to ``x[1]`` (in the first graph's coordinates).
Between.title: Between

DifferenceOf.description: The first area without the others.
DifferenceOf.title: DifferenceOf

Ellipse.description: An axis-aligned ellipse with radii ``rx`` and ``ry``; turn it with a group.
Ellipse.title: Ellipse

FloodFill.description:
The part of the plane around ``seed`` that the lines of ``bounded_by`` enclose.

Like a paint bucket: the boundaries may be open lines (a parabola, a
line and an axis); together they must close the part the seed is in.
It is not outlined unless it gives a ``color``.
FloodFill.title: FloodFill

Group.description:
Objects that move together.

``children`` are ids of other objects. The transform scales and rotates
them about ``pivot`` (degrees, counterclockwise), then translates them;
it turns and scales their drawings too, strokes and texts included. The
group's opacity multiplies each child's.
Group.title: Group

HalfPlane.description: Everything to the left of the line through two points, going from the first to the second.
HalfPlane.title: HalfPlane

Label.description:
A text or formula that belongs to a shape and is drawn beside one of its points.

``at`` names the owner's anchor (``"tip"``, ``"center"``, ``"right_top"``).
With ``dir`` the label sits beside that point, ``gap`` away; without it,
it is centered on the point. It is drawn as the object ``<owner>.label``,
in the owner's color unless it says otherwise, at the ``label`` size.
Label.title: Label

Math.description:
A formula in TeX, set in display style and placed like a text.

``tex`` is what goes between the dollars: ``"\frac{a}{b}"``. The
front-end typesets it before anything is drawn, so a TeX mistake is
reported (E-TEX) with this object's path.
Math.title: Math

Mix.description: An extra color mixed from two others, for example the overlap of two concepts.
Mix.title: Mix

OnRef.description:
A point on an object's outline: ``t`` of the way along it, or where it reaches ``x``.

``t`` runs from 0 at the start to 1 at the end, by length. ``x`` is in the
object's own coordinates (its space, if it has one); the first point in
drawing order that reaches it is taken.
OnRef.title: OnRef

Path.description: Straight and Bezier segments, in one or more subpaths (holes are subpaths).
Path.title: Path

Polygon.description: A closed outline through ``points``, in order.
Polygon.title: Polygon

Polyline.description: An open line through ``points``, in order.
Polyline.title: Polyline

Rect.description: An axis-aligned rectangle; turn it with a group.
Rect.title: Rect

Region.description:
An area built from other shapes: ``{"difference": ["A", "B"]}`` (regions.py).

Its operands are often defs, which are not drawn themselves. A region is
not outlined unless it gives a ``color``.
Region.title: Region

RegularPolygon.description:
``sides`` corners on a circle of ``radius`` around ``center``.

With ``rotation`` 0 it stands on a flat bottom edge (a triangle points up,
a square is axis-aligned); ``rotation`` turns it counterclockwise.
RegularPolygon.title: RegularPolygon

RoleSizes.description: Type size of each text role, in reference pixels.
RoleSizes.title: RoleSizes

Sector.description: A slice of a disc: the arc from ``start_angle`` to ``end_angle`` and two radii.
Sector.title: Sector

Space.description:
A coordinate system objects can be drawn in with ``"in": "<id>"`` (analysis §2.3).

A point (x, y) of the space is drawn at ``origin + (x * ux, y * uy)``,
where ``unit`` is ``ux`` (and ``uy``) frame units per space unit; lengths
scale the same way. Stroke widths and type sizes do not. ``origin`` may
be a reference (``"safe.center"``). ``kind`` leaves room for 3D later
(analysis §5).
Space.title: Space

Stack.description:
Objects laid out in a column, a row or a grid, as one box (analysis §2.8).

``children`` are ids of other objects, in reading order; a grid fills
rows of ``columns`` children, left to right, top to bottom. Each child
sits in its cell so that its ``align`` point meets the cell's: ``left_center``
lines a column up on the left, ``center_baseline`` a row on its
baselines. ``spacing`` is the room between cells: one number, or
``[between columns, between rows]``. The stack itself is placed like a
text; its baseline is its first row's.
Stack.title: Stack

Style.description: A style class: any paint or text field, applied to every object that names it.
Style.title: Style

Subpath.description: One pen stroke: a start point and the segments that follow it.
Subpath.title: Subpath

SubtitleHeader.description: The subtitle setting and, unless the mode is ``none``, the band it keeps.
SubtitleHeader.title: SubtitleHeader

ThemeHeader.description:
What an object gets when neither it nor its style classes say (analysis §2.8).

A color left out here is white or black, whichever contrasts more with
the background.
ThemeHeader.title: ThemeHeader

Under.description: Between a graph and the line y = 0 of its own coordinates, from ``x[0]`` to ``x[1]``.
Under.title: Under

XorOf.description: Where exactly one of the two areas is.
XorOf.title: XorOf

title: IRDocument
